reason: Every element checks out. The cited AUS release (https://www.aus.edu/node/121001, 6 Nov 2025) states that Team Hayyakum won first place and AED 20,000 for "Sharjah Quest," lists members Mahmoud Darwish, Amr Mohi Aldeen, Mohamad Dabbagh, and Afif Zughayer, and describes an "augmented reality-powered mobile adventure" with a digital passport, stamps and badges, leaderboards, curated itineraries, heritage mascots, and citywide challenges, plus the sentence "Real-time guidance spreads footfall, increases dwell time and supports neighborhood businesses." The independent Sharjah24 report (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2025/11/06/Innovation-Hackathon-reimagines-tourism-experience-at-AUS) repeats the same team, prize, member names, and feature list verbatim. "Last year" is correct: the 2025 edition ran 1-2 November 2025 and the 2026 edition runs 10-11 October 2026 (https://auscse.com/hackathon/). The mentor overlap is supported by the project's organizer-derived brief (D:\Sharjah Tourism Hackathon\00_Hackathon_Brief.md, compiled 10 Oct 2026 from the organizer's Mentor Profiles deck), which lists Afif Zughayer (Founder, Amana Vision) and Mahmoud Darwish (Founder, ReteIntel) among the eight 2026 mentors. Limitation: no public web page names the 2026 mentors (the auscse.com page names none, and web searches for the two names with their affiliations return nothing), so that half rests on the organizer documents rather than a public source; the claim's careful wording ("share names with") is appropriate, since no source establishes they are the same people. "Spreads visitor traffic" is a fair paraphrase of "spreads footfall."
